notes.meaning: The writer turns away from earthly troubles to look up at God, who rules over all from heaven. When human help fails, believers find comfort knowing their King sits on a heavenly throne far above any earthly power. Looking upward reminds us that God has all the help and mercy we need.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine taught that all believers speak here as one body in Christ, lifting their hearts toward God rather than being proud, with heaven representing the holy souls in whom God lives.

notes.meaning: In ancient times, servants watched their master's hand closely for quiet signals telling them what to do, or looked to that hand for food and protection. Believers watch the Lord with the same humble, patient trust, waiting for His help against those who mistreat them. They choose to keep their eyes fixed on God until His mercy arrives.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine viewed the servant and maid as believers and the Church, with Christ as both Master and divine Wisdom, looking faithfully toward Him during life's journey.

notes.meaning: God's people repeat their cry for mercy because their pain is great and they need help urgently. They have endured so much mockery and disrespect from their enemies that they are completely full of sorrow. Instead of claiming they deserve rescue, they simply throw themselves on God's kindness.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine taught that anyone living a godly life will be despised by worldly people, since believers hope for heavenly promises they cannot yet see.

notes.meaning: The ones doing the mocking are proud people who live in ease and care nothing for God's laws. Being surrounded by comfortable, arrogant enemies who look down on God's servants is deeply painful to bear. Even so, God's people find quiet confidence knowing that the Lord's mercy will outlast the pride of their oppressors.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine explained that the wealthy and proud include those who boast in their own righteousness; while they mock Christians today, they will face deep regret in the judgment.
